gaps.sentence: Do you fancy ___ to the cinema tonight?
gaps.explanation: fancy + -ing (informal British): Do you fancy going…?

gaps.sentence: You risk ___ your licence if you drink and drive.
I resent ___ treated as an amateur when I have twenty years’ experience.
gaps.explanation: 'Resent' takes a gerund; the passive is 'being treated'.

gaps.sentence: I remembered ___ the door, so I went back to check.
gaps.explanation: remember + -ing = recall a past action; remember to do = not forget a duty.
can't stand + -ing (also to-infinitive in AmE): can't stand waiting. -ing accepted as standard.

gaps.sentence: She keeps ___ about the exam results.
Despite ___ three times, he didn't give up.
On the way to Rome we stopped ___ some photos.
gaps.hint: stop in order to do sth
gaps.explanation: stop to do = pause in order to do; stop doing = finish doing. Here they paused to take photos.
